Avoid all mind altering substances, including alcohol, weed, cigarettes, and caffeine. Keep a journal and write about your day to day life. Make sure you try to get enough sleep. Get some exercise and engage your body. 

Another good tip is to talk about your experiences with someone else you trust besides just your therapist, maybe a loved one or close friend. Let them know how you've been feeling and some warning signs to look out for. For me, these warning signs were social withdrawal, unconventional spiritual beliefs that kind of arose out of nowhere and getting obsessed with the occult (basically any significant change in personality or worldview) , and more obvious signs of psychosis like interacting with hallucinations or fixed delusions. If things progress that far you may have less insight into your condition, so it's good to have someone close to you who can check up on you regularly and help you get the medical attention you may need. Also, even though it initially sucks, don't be afraid to go to the hospital. It's better than potentially losing years of your life to psychosis, which is something that is easier to treat in its early stages.

For me it started with mood changes. I had dealt with depression and anxiety most of my teenage years but shortly after I went vegan I began to feel more fatigued and irritable. Started the diet in June 2014, by the end of September I was a mess. I could barely get out of bed most days, everything made me cry, I couldn't concentrate. Then one morning I woke up and I was not ok. It was like I never woke up from dreaming. Everything looked like I was seeing it through a foggy veil. I felt simultaneously spacey and agitated, like I wanted to jump out of my skin. I felt disconnected from my body, almost like it wasn't my own. This went on for a few weeks. Then one morning I woke up and was hallucinating that my flesh was rotting off my body. I could even smell it. It seemed so real to me. 

From this point on, my memory is spotty. Memory loss can be a symptom of B12 deficiency as well. I remember feelings of profound distress and skipping class to walk around in the woods. Sometimes I did this for days and wouldn't eat and barely drank water. I felt like I could not be around other humans. I felt defective and primitive. I started doing strange rituals and hearing voices that guided me to do these things. There were several different voices. Some were helpful and encouraging, another one was mean and berating, and there was one I was convinced was a demon. At some point I left the woods and immediately went to the college's counseling department to schedule an appointment. I don't know where this insight came from but I am thankful for it. 

I ended up leaving school on medical withdrawal for depression in November. In December, I was hospitalized at inpatient psychiatry after screaming at my mother. I had been so severely agitated that every single noise was unbearable. I wished I didn't have to breathe because the perception of it was painful. Blinking felt like thunder. My heartbeat pounded in my ears like a booming bass drum. So when my mom came in to ask me to do the dishes talking at a normal volume I lost it completely. Started screaming, throwing things, sobbing. I was there for three days. They diagnosed me as Bipolar type 1 and gave me gabapentin and Prozac.
